challenges.title: The midday work ban from 15 June to 15 September

items.title: The midday ban on outdoor work
items.text: From 15 June to 15 September, work in direct sunlight or in the open air is banned every day from 12:30 to 15:00 — a rule that hits outdoor and window cleaning directly (an annual MOHRE ministerial decision, now in its 22nd year in 2026).

items.title: Fines of up to AED 50,000 per breach
items.text: Breaches cost AED 5,000 per affected employee, capped at AED 50,000 — on top of that, a company faces a file freeze and downgrading.

items.title: Split shifts instead of a midday gap
items.text: To stop the banned window turning into dead time, cleaning teams need to redistribute their shifts across the morning and late afternoon.

solutions.title: How Klacks takes the load off facility and cleaning services in the UAE
solutions.subtitle: From the automatic block to split-shift planning — everything works together.

items.title: The midday window blocked automatically
items.text: Klacks automatically blocks outdoor and window-cleaning shifts between 12:30 and 15:00 from 15 June to 15 September — every year, with no need to re-enter the dates by hand.

items.title: The AED 50,000 fine risk avoided
items.text: Because the banned window can never be scheduled in the first place, the risk of the AED 5,000 fine per employee simply doesn't arise.

items.title: Sites & routes automatically optimised
items.text: Klacks plans cleaning routes between sites so that journeys stay short and time windows are met.

items.title: Split shifts suggested automatically
items.text: Klacks suggests shifts before and after the banned window, so the day's working hours still add up.

items.title: On-premise: full data sovereignty
items.text: Klacks runs on your own infrastructure — your cleaning team's personal data never leaves your organisation.

items.title: Klacksy schedules by voice
items.text: "Split tomorrow's outdoor cleaning across morning and afternoon" is all it takes — Klacksy automatically observes the midday ban.

example.title: The midday ban and the split shift, at a glance
example.text: Klacks automatically recognises when an outdoor-cleaning shift between 15 June and 15 September falls within the banned window of 12:30 to 15:00, and immediately suggests a split shift before and after it — no manual recalculating required.
